chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan that he wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who sold his estate to another man, and it was a piece of land, and the boundaries were not defined at the time he called witnesses, and he said, 'When they bring you the boundaries, then bear witness with them.' Is that allowed for him, or is it not allowed for him to testify?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Yes, it is allowed, and the praise is to Allah.'

And a man wrote to him who had a piece of land. So he was preparing to depart for Mecca, and the town was a few stages from his house, and he did not bring the boundaries of his land, but he defined the four boundaries of the town. So he said to the witnesses, 'Bear witness that I have sold to so-and-so the entirety of the town, whose one boundary is such-and-such, and the second, and the third, and the fourth.' But rather, for him in this town was only a piece of land. So is that correct for the buyer, when for him was only part of this town, and he acknowledged for him the entirety of it?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'It is not allowed to sell what one does not own, and the purchase is obligatory upon the seller according to what he owns.'

And he wrote, 'Is it allowed for the witness whom he called to witness with the entirety of this town that he testifies with the boundaries of the piece of land which is for him in it, when the boundaries of this piece are recognized by a people from the inhabitants of this town, if they are just?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Yes, they testify upon something understood and known.'

And a man wrote, 'A man says to a man, 'Bear witness that the entirety of the house which is for him in such-and-such a place, with all its boundaries, is for so-and-so son of so-and-so, and the entirety of what is for him in the house from the chattels.' Is that correct for the buyer, whatever is in the house from the chattels, which things are they?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'It is correct for him whatever the purchase encompassed of all that, if Allah wills.'

key_terms.بَيْعُ مَا لَيْسَ يَمْلِكُ: Selling what one does not own

ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic legal rulings on selling land or property when the exact boundaries are not yet defined or when the seller owns only a part of a larger area?
ai.summary: Imam al-Hadi (AS) clarifies the validity of selling undivided shares or specific portions within a larger defined entity, emphasizing that the sale is binding on what the seller actually owns. The text highlights the scholarly principle that witnesses can testify to specific boundaries if they are clearly understood, even if not explicitly detailed in the initial contract, and extends this validity to movable goods within a property. This reflects the Shia juristic approach to resolving ambiguity in property transactions by focusing on the actual ownership and clear identification of the subject matter.
